methodologyNotes: Covers standalone on-camera flashes (speedlights / flashguns) and compact hot-shoe strobes sold at a published US price. Excludes bare studio monolights, built-in pop-up flashes, LED continuous lights, ring lights, and off-camera-only heads that lack a hot-shoe foot. Price is typical US retail or MSRP in USD. guideNumberM is the guide number in meters at ISO 100 measured at the head's maximum zoom setting (higher = more power). zoomRangeMm is the motorized zoom coverage as min-max full-frame-equivalent focal length in mm. recycleTimeSec is the manufacturer full-power recycle time in seconds (lower is better). fullPowerFlashes is the rated number of full-power pops per fully charged pack or fresh set of cells. colorTempKelvin is nominal flash color temperature in Kelvin; null if not disclosed. wirelessSystem is the built-in wireless triggering type: "2.4ghz-radio", "optical", or "none". highSpeedSync is true if the flash supports HSS / FP sync above the camera's native sync speed. ttlSupport is true if it supports through-the-lens auto exposure for at least one camera system. batteryType is the primary power source: "li-ion" (dedicated lithium pack), "4xaa" (four AA cells), or "proprietary". headRotationDeg is the maximum horizontal swivel of the bounce head in degrees. roundHead is true if the flash uses a round / circular light head. weightGrams is body weight in grams excluding batteries.

Sourced verbatim from the PetaPixel dated review (2024-04-04): "The recently released $329 Godox V1 Pro..." and "The $329 Godox V1 Pro is available for Canon, Nikon, Sony, Fujifilm, and Olympus camera systems." The official Godox manufacturer page does not list a price.
products.provenance: The official Godox product page (godox.com/product-b/V1Pro.html) confirms the exact "V1Pro" model across all mount variants (C/N/S/F/O) and supplies the spec sheet: 76Ws power, 28-105mm flash coverage, 0-330° horizontal swivel, Radio 2.4G wireless, high-speed sync to 1/8000s, E-TTL II/i-TTL/TTL, built-in 7.2V lithium battery, ~1.3s recycle time, and ~500 full-power flashes. The dated PetaPixel review (2024-04-04) corroborates the same model and specs (76W, 330-degree swivel, 28-105mm zoom, 100 continuous full-power shots) and states the US price twice as "$329." No guide number is disclosed on the manufacturer page, and the only Kelvin figure (3300K±200K) explicitly refers to the LED modeling lamp rather than the flash discharge, so both guideNumberM and colorTempKelvin are left null; the reviews' "580 grams" reads as a total (battery-included) figure, so the excluding-batteries weight is also null.
